page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: What it separates
lines: It is used for a volatile liquid mixed
with a non-volatile impurity, and for
two liquids whose boiling points differ
The liquid with the lower boiling point
steps.why: The two cases are really one case. A non-volatile impurity has almost no vapour pressure, and a liquid boiling more than about 40 °C higher has very little, so in both the vapour that comes off is nearly all the more volatile component.
common_mistakes: Saying distillation separates any two liquids. The boiling points must differ by more than about 40 °C.
Saying it purifies solids. It is a method for liquids.
steps.memory_tip: Two cases: a non-volatile impurity, or a boiling point gap wider than about 40 °C.
steps.margin_note: State both cases in the opening lines, and give the 40 °C figure as a number.

steps.label: Boiling, condensing and collecting
lines: The mixture is boiled in a distillation
The vapour is led into a condenser,
where it is cooled back to a liquid,
and this distillate is collected in a
steps.why: Boiling turns the more volatile liquid into vapour and leaves the rest in the flask; condensing turns that vapour back into a liquid in a different vessel. The separation happens because those two changes are made to occur in two different places.
common_mistakes: Stopping at boiling. Without the condenser the vapour is lost and nothing is collected.
Giving aniline as the distillate. Benzene has the lower boiling point, so benzene comes over first.
steps.memory_tip: Boil it in one vessel and condense it in another, and the two liquids end up in different places.
steps.margin_note: Write both boiling points with the example. One closing line naming which liquid distils first completes the answer.

insider_note: Two marks, so two things: the two cases the method covers with the 40 °C figure, and the sequence boil, condense, collect. A named pair of liquids with their boiling points, such as benzene at 80 °C and aniline at 184 °C, turns a bare definition into a full answer.
